entries.original: A far i fat su an s'insporca mai el man.
entries.literal_it: Facendo i fatti propri non ci si sporca mai le mani.
entries.meaning_it: Chi si fa i fatti suoi non si mette nei guai.
entries.meaning_en: Mind your own business and you stay out of trouble.
entries.usage_context: interfering in a colleague's mess, staying out of other people's quarrels
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Al bón vein al n'ha bisógn dla frasca.
entries.literal_it: Il buon vino non ha bisogno della frasca.
entries.meaning_it: La qualità non ha bisogno di pubblicità (la frasca era l'insegna dell'osteria).
entries.meaning_en: Good wine needs no bush: quality needs no advertising.
entries.usage_context: praising good work, a clean solution that needs no fanfare
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Al prem còulp an casca l'alber.
entries.literal_it: Al primo colpo non cade l'albero.
entries.meaning_it: Per riuscire serve insistere, spesso più tentativi.
entries.meaning_en: The tree does not fall at the first blow: persistence is needed.
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Al vén l'è la tatta di vîc.
entries.literal_it: Il vino è il biberon dei vecchi.
entries.meaning_it: Il vino è il latte dei vecchi.
entries.meaning_en: Wine is the old men's baby bottle.
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Anch quésta l'è fatta, dess quél ch' cavò i uc' a so muier.
entries.literal_it: Anche questa è fatta, disse quello che cavò gli occhi alla moglie.
entries.meaning_it: Si dice (ironicamente) quando si porta a termine un lavoro con soddisfazione.
entries.meaning_en: Another job done, said the man who put out his wife's eyes (wellerism).
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ. Black-humour wellerism: use sparingly.

entries.original: Andar alla bassa, tòt i sant ajuten.
entries.literal_it: Andando alla bassa (a favore), tutti i santi aiutano.
entries.meaning_it: Quando le cose vanno per il verso giusto tutti danno una mano.
entries.meaning_en: When things go downhill (with the wind) every saint helps.
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ. The wording is partly Italianate.

entries.original: Com dess la vóulp ol u: zò l'an me pias.
entries.literal_it: Come disse la volpe all'uva: ...
entries.meaning_it: Detto di chi finge di disprezzare ciò che desidera (l'uva acerba).
entries.meaning_en: As the fox said of the grapes: pretending to scorn what one wants.
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ. The printed text looks garbled ('ol u'): reproduced as given, low confidence in the exact words.

entries.original: Cum dess quél ch' frava el i och, ai vol ésser da far.
entries.literal_it: Come disse quello che ferrava le oche: c'è da fare.
entries.meaning_it: Si dice di un compito quasi impossibile (ferrare le oche).
entries.meaning_en: As the man shoeing geese said: there is work to do (an almost impossible task).
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ. The printed text looks garbled: reproduced as given, low confidence in the exact words.

entries.original: Dal det al fat ai é un gran trat.
entries.literal_it: Dal detto al fatto c'è un gran tratto.
entries.meaning_it: Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo un gran tratto.
entries.meaning_en: Between saying and doing there is a long way.
entries.usage_context: promises vs delivery, 'it will be ready tomorrow'
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Du gal in t'un pullar i stan mal.
entries.literal_it: Due galli in un pollaio stanno male.
entries.meaning_it: Due rivali per la stessa cosa non vanno d'accordo.
entries.meaning_en: Two cocks in one henhouse do not get along.
entries.usage_context: two senior devs on one decision, rivalry
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Quand la bèrba fà al stupén lâsa äl dòn e tént al vén.
entries.literal_it: Quando la barba fa lo stoppino, lascia le donne e tieni il vino.
entries.meaning_it: Invecchiando si rinuncia alle donne e si preferisce il vino.
entries.meaning_en: With white beard, leave women and keep to wine.
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ. Sexist-leaning old saying: quote rather than apply.

entries.original: Méi al vén féss che l'âcua cèra.
entries.literal_it: Meglio il vino torbido che l'acqua chiara.
entries.meaning_it: Detto dei bevitori: meglio un vino torbido dell'acqua limpida.
entries.meaning_en: Murky wine beats clear water (drinkers' saying).
entries.usage_context: jokes among friends at the osteria
entries.notes: Spelling is quoted as printed on Wikiquote, which mixes 19th-century (Coronedi Berti) and modern forms; the modern OLM spelling of some words may differ.

entries.original: Al pan di èter l é sèt gràsst.
entries.literal_it: Il pane degli altri è sapido/salato.
entries.meaning_it: Rendering of Dante's 'sa di sale lo pane altrui': vivere alle spalle altrui è amaro.
entries.meaning_en: Others' bread tastes of salt: depending on others is hard.
entries.usage_context: dependence on someone else's infrastructure or favours
entries.notes: Called a 'proverbio petroniano' on bulgnais.com. The exact spelling and the reading rest on a garbled page, and the line may be a literary translation rather than traditional wording: low confidence.

entries.original: stèr in uràccia
entries.literal_it: stare in orecchia
entries.meaning_it: Stare all'erta, sul chi vive.
entries.meaning_en: To be on one's guard.

entries.original: fèr al fûrb
entries.literal_it: fare il furbo
entries.meaning_it: Comportarsi da furbo, fare lo scaltro.
entries.meaning_en: To act smart.
entries.notes: Attested as part of a sample sentence (l é un èṡen es vôl fèr al fûrb).

entries.original: Sòccmel!
entries.literal_it: succhiamelo
entries.meaning_it: Esclamazione di stupore, ammirazione o disappunto.
entries.meaning_en: Bolognese all-purpose exclamation.
entries.usage_context: any surprise; never as a formal phrase
entries.notes: See profanity.json for the cruder extensions.

entries.original: dòvv as dìs sèmper sòccmel
entries.literal_it: dove si dice sempre socmel
entries.meaning_it: Umoristica resa bolognese del 'dove il sì suona' di Dante (Bologna come terra del socmel).
entries.meaning_en: Humorous Bolognese rendering of Dante's 'where the sì sounds'.
entries.usage_context: quoting Bologna as the land of socmel
entries.notes: From a page snippet read in a garbled encoding; treat as a literary pun, not a traditional saying.

entries.original: prilèr la maṡèla
entries.literal_it: far girare la manovella
entries.meaning_it: Fare sempre la stessa cosa, ripetitivamente.
entries.meaning_en: To do the same thing over and over.
entries.notes: The bulgnais corso page glosses it as 'fare una cosa sempre uguale'; the exact diacritics on the verb were lost to encoding.

entries.original: fare balotta
entries.literal_it: fare balotta
entries.meaning_it: Passare la serata insieme agli amici.
entries.meaning_en: To hang out with friends.
entries.notes: Regional Italian, not dialect proper: use inside Italian-flavoured sentences.

entries.original: Mi suda anche la lingua in bocca
entries.literal_it: mi suda anche la lingua in bocca
entries.meaning_it: Fa un caldo eccessivo.
entries.meaning_en: It is boiling hot (even my tongue sweats).

entries.original: andare a busso
entries.literal_it: andare a busso
entries.meaning_it: Andare a tutta velocità.
entries.meaning_en: To go flat out.

entries.original: buttare il rusco
entries.literal_it: buttare il rusco
entries.meaning_it: Buttare la spazzatura.
entries.meaning_en: To take out the rubbish.

entries.original: dare il tiro
entries.literal_it: dare il tiro
entries.meaning_it: Aprire il portone col citofono.
entries.meaning_en: To buzz someone in.

entries.original: bóna lé
entries.literal_it: buona là
entries.meaning_it: Basta così, la misura è colma.
entries.meaning_en: Enough is enough.
